info.title: NetPace
info.description: Cross-platform network speed testing CLI. Measures latency, download and upload speed against Ookla Speedtest servers, with human-readable, CSV and JSON output.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription:
Network speed tester including server discovery, latency measurement, download
and upload speed testing.

commands.name: ENVIRONMENT
commands.description: Network speed tester including server discovery, latency measurement, download and upload speed testing.

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --loop
options.description: Performs the speed test on continuous loop.

options.name: --count
options.description: Stop speed testing after this many times. [default: 1]

options.name: --delay
options.description: Time between multiple speed tests (HH:MM:SS). [default: 00:00:00]

options.name: --time-limit
options.description:
Stop a speed test run after this long (HH:MM:SS, up to 23:59:59).
A run that reaches the limit reports what it measured up to then.
Each run of --count or --loop gets the limit afresh, and --delay is not counted. [default: 00:10:00]

options.name: --csv
options.description: Display output as a single CSV row (always includes timestamp).

options.name: --no-csv-header
options.description:
Do not write the header row (CSV output only).
An appended --file target that already holds rows is never sent the header.

options.name: --json
options.description: Display output in Json format.

options.name: --json-pretty
options.description: Display output in Json format (pretty print).

options.name: --minimal
options.description:
Display the result as a single timestamped line per run.
Ideal for watching repeated runs with --loop or --count.

options.name: --simple
options.description:
Display the result as one named line per figure: Ping, Download, Upload.
Ideal for batch scripts and line-based parsing.

options.name: --no-latency
options.description:
Do not perform latency test.
When used without --server-url, the first available server is selected.

options.name: --no-download
options.description: Do not perform download test.

options.name: --no-upload
options.description: Do not perform upload test.

options.name: --provider
options.description:
The kind of server to test against. <ookla, librespeed>
'librespeed' needs --server-url naming where LibreSpeed is installed. [default: Ookla]

options.name: --server-url
options.description:
The URL of a specific speed test server.
'netpace servers -l' will return your nearest servers.
With --provider librespeed, the address LibreSpeed is installed at.

options.name: --profile
options.description: Profile bundle of payload settings. <tiny, small, medium, large, mega> [default: Medium]

options.name: --downloadsize
options.description: Stop the download test after this many megabytes (IEC MiB). [default: 2147483647]

options.name: --uploadsize
options.description: Stop the upload test after this many megabytes (IEC MiB). [default: 2147483647]

options.name: --connections
options.description:
Maximum transfers the download and upload tests each run at once (1-32).
Overrides the --profile connection count; the profile's data caps still apply.
A maximum, so a profile with fewer transfers to run than this will not reach it.

options.name: --unit
options.description:
The speed unit. <bits, bytes>
Applies to the default, minimal and simple output. [default: BitsPerSecond]

options.name: --unit-scale
options.description:
The speed unit scale. <auto, base, kilo, mega, giga, tera, peta>
Applies to the default, minimal and simple output. [default: Auto]

options.name: --unit-system
options.description:
The speed unit system. <SI, IEC>
Applies to the default, minimal and simple output.
SI steps up in powers of 1000 (KB, MB, GB), common in networking,
while IEC uses powers of 1024 (KiB, MiB, GiB), standard in computing and storage. [default: SI]

options.name: --device-id
options.description:
Record a label for this machine in CSV and JSON output.
The CSV column is always present; the JSON field appears only when a label is given.

options.name: --custom-field
options.description:
Record a key=value pair in CSV and JSON output.
May be given more than once, and is recorded in the order given.

options.name: --file
options.description: Write output to file.

options.name: --file-mode
options.description: Determines file output behavior. <append, overwrite> [default: Append]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress all normal console output (file output still works).

options.name: --fail-on
--min-download
options.description:
Exit 3 when the download speed is below this, such as 50Mbps.
Takes any unit NetPace writes a speed in, whatever --unit, --unit-system and --unit-scale say.
Checks one run, so not with --loop, --count above 1, or --no-download.

options.name: --min-upload
options.description:
Exit 3 when the upload speed is below this, such as 50Mbps.
Read the same way as --min-download; not with --loop, --count above 1, or --no-upload.

options.name: --max-latency
options.description:
Exit 3 when the idle latency is above this, such as 40ms.
Milliseconds only; not with --loop, --count above 1, or --no-latency.

options.name: --diagnostics
options.description:
Write per-request diagnostic detail about the run to the error stream.
The result is unchanged, so 'netpace --json --diagnostics > result.json 2> diagnostics.log' keeps the two apart.

options.name: --diagnostics-file
options.description:
Write the diagnostic detail to this file instead of the error stream.
Turns diagnostics on by itself, and replaces the file on every run.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

commands.description: Show the nearest speed test servers.

options.name: --latency
options.description: Include server latency in the results.

options.name: --fastest
options.description: Show the fastest server details, selected by lowest latency.
